result.note: Tests the main provisions of the RBI's June 2026 draft guidelines on AI and model risk in banks.

questions.prompt: In June 2026, the Reserve Bank of India released draft guidelines on model risk, including artificial intelligence, in banks. Consider the following statements about the draft:
items: Every lender would have to adopt a board-approved framework covering all models, with AI and machine learning explicitly in scope.
Models sourced from third parties would be exempt from independent validation.
Generative AI that interacts with customers would carry extra cybersecurity controls.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the draft subjects third-party models to independent validation rather than exempting them. The draft also requires human oversight of AI used in automated decisions, and the RBI invited feedback by 24 July.
questions.source: Third-party models would face independent validation, AI used in automated decisions would need human oversight, and generative AI that interacts with customers would carry extra cybersecurity controls.
